title: Choosing a Trajectory Generator
summary: Work through Choosing a Trajectory Generator.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Choosing a Trajectory Generator** in *Trajectory Planning* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Trajectory Planning, § Choosing a Trajectory Generator
blocks.md: When a mobile manipulator reaches around a conveyor guard, a planner that searches configuration space can run out of time before finding a route. A local trajectory optimizer can get trapped in a non-convex pocket behind the guard. A learned action-chunk policy can propose a smooth reach that clips the guard or exceeds a joint's torque limit. The three algorithmic families that propose motion, geometric search, continuous optimization, and learned action chunking, each fail in a different way if treated as self-certifying.

options: A collision-free path is executable only if every joint's position, velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque, and current stay within limits along the continuous interpolant, its seams, and its stop, which time parameterization must check.

The planner hands over an immutable record naming frame, evidence epoch, seam state, parent intent-lease digest, and four MCU-clock deadlines in two tiers (high-rate chunk lease, hardware commitment cutoff) together with its latched stop.
A differential-drive base reaches the same configurations as a holonomic one but through a restricted velocity space, so it plans over controls.
Planning searches the configuration space and its collision-free subset, and collision queries dominate a sampling planner's run time.
